texts.preamble: Vinod Kumar vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 4 December, 2023 Author: Sushrut Arvind Dharmadhikari Bench: Sushrut Arvind Dharmadhikari, Pranay Verma 1 In The High Court Of Madhya Pradesh At Indore Before Hon'Ble Shri Justice Sushrut Arvind Dharmadhikari & Hon'Ble Shri Justice Pranay Verma On The 4 th Of December, 2023 Writ Appeal No. 2183 of 2023 Between:- Vinod Kumar S/O Kishanlal Jain, Aged About 60 Year S , Occupation: Business Jawahar Marg, Nagda Tehsil Nagda District Ujjain (Madhya Pradesh) .... ( Shri Sanjay Kumar Bahirani, Advocate Appearing On Behalf Of Appellant Through V.C .) And 1. The State Of Madhya Pradesh Principal Secretary Food Safety And Drug Administration Department Vallabh Bhawan District Bhopal (Madhya Pradesh) 2. Collector Dist. Ujjain (Madhya Pradesh) 3. Designated Officer Food And Drug Administration Department Ujjain (Madhya Pradesh) 4. Food Safety Officer Basant Sharma Food And Drug Administration Department Ujjain (Madhya Pradesh) .....R
texts.facts: 2. Brief facts of the case are that appellant is a Mawa vendor and 55 buckets of Mawa weighing 1375 kg were seized from the Cold Storage and three samples were sent for testing. The appellant has filed an application before the competent authority seeking release of seized M a w a on supurdginama which was disposed off vide order dated 14.07.2023 with the pre-condition to deposit Rs. 3,43,000/- in the form of demand draft/bank guarantee with the further condition that the third sample of Mawa sent for test at Referral Food Laboratory, Mysore if found to be contrary to the standard laid down under the Food Safety Act , the demand draft/bank guarantee so deposited shall be encashed. Against the said order, appellant has preferred writ petition which was dismissed by the order impugned by the learned Single Judge. Now the present intra Court appeal is filed.
texts.arguments: 3. Learned counsel for the appellant submitted that learned Single has passed the order on wrong consideration of facts, law and contrary to the record of the case. Learned Single Judge has erred in not considering that as per Section 46(3) of the Food Safety Act and Rule 4.2.5 and 4.2.6 of the Food Safety Rules which provides that on receipt of the sample, the food analyst shall forward the report within 14 days and in case in such time sample is not tested then food analyst shall inform to the designated officers and Food Commissioner giving and specifying the time taken in the analysis which has not been done in the present case. It is further submitted that food samples were collected from only 03 buckets. However, entire 55 buckets of Ma wa were seized. Moreso, while testing third sample which has been tested as per the regulation 2.1.6 of Food Safety and Standard (Food Product Standards and Food Additives) Regulation, 2011[referred to as 'the Regulation 2011], the referral Food Laboratory Mysore did not mention about the formalin test which is used for preserving food article then in absence of particular test, it cannot be accepted that the sample of Mawa which has been tested by the Referral Food Laboratory was fit for test analysis. Hence, the said report cannot be relied upon.
